sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: In this lesson one small word, will, does a lot of work: a guess about tomorrow, a decision you make on the spot, a promise, an offer of help. At the end you will choose between will, going to and the -ing form from lesson 15.

examples.en: I think the heatwave will end tomorrow.
I'll get the plunger.
I'll keep in touch.
Shall I cool down the soup?

blocks.text: When you guess how things will be, say will + the action as in the dictionary. Will is the same for everyone: I will, he will, they will. It often comes after I think: this is your opinion, not a plan.

examples.en: I think the humidity will rise.
examples.translation: the air will get more damp

examples.en: I think the mist will clear soon.
I think I will oversleep tomorrow.
examples.translation: I will wake up too late

examples.en: I think they will overcharge us.

fixes.wrong: I think the humidity will to rise.
fixes.right: I think the humidity will rise.

fixes.wrong: I think the humidity will rises.
fixes.right: I think the humidity will rise.

drill.why: After will comes the action as in the dictionary: no to, no -s.

sections.title: will be — how something will be

blocks.text: When it is not an action but a state — the beach full of people, the tea not hot enough — put be after will: will be overcrowded, will be lukewarm. Do not leave be out and do not use is.

examples.en: I think it will be overcast tomorrow.
I think the beach will be overcrowded.
I think the tea will be lukewarm.
I think the soup will be scalding.

fixes.wrong: I think the beach will overcrowded.
fixes.right: I think the beach will be overcrowded.

fixes.wrong: I think the beach will is overcrowded.
fixes.right: I think the beach will be overcrowded.

blocks.text: I'll is the short form of I will. The water is not going down the sink, you have just noticed, and you decide on the spot: I'll get the plunger. You did not plan it before; the decision is made this second.

examples.en: I'll get the plunger.
I'll get a tablespoon.
I'll roll up my sleeves.
I'll mop up the water.
examples.translation: there is water on the floor

examples.en: I'll fill up the water bottle.

drill.question: The water is not going down the sink. You have just noticed. What do you say?
drill.explain: A decision about the future, made right now: I'll.

blocks.text: The same I'll makes a promise: your friend is going away and is worried about their mother, so you reassure them — I'll check in on your mother. The form is the same; the situation gives the meaning.

examples.en: I'll check in on your mother.
examples.translation: I will see that she is OK

examples.en: I'll keep in touch.
I'll drop by tomorrow.
examples.translation: I will visit for a short time

examples.en: I'll hand in the form tomorrow.
I'll keep an eye on your bag.
examples.translation: I will watch it for you

sections.title: I'll and Shall I…? — offering help

blocks.text: You can offer help in two ways. Just do it: I'll top up your glass. Or ask if it is wanted: Shall I cool down the soup? After Shall I comes the action as in the dictionary, with no to and no second will.

examples.en: I'll top up your glass.
examples.translation: I will add more to it

examples.en: Shall I cool down the soup?
Shall I clear away the plates?
Shall I put up the shelf?
Shall I come round this evening?
examples.translation: do you want me to visit?

fixes.wrong: Shall I to cool down the soup?
fixes.right: Shall I cool down the soup?

fixes.wrong: Shall I will cool down the soup?
fixes.right: Shall I cool down the soup?

drill.prompt: Offer to cut the bread into pieces.

blocks.text: Three ways to talk about the future, each with its own shade. You think it will happen: will. You decided earlier: going to. You agreed with someone and there is a time: -ing. Sometimes they overlap; choose the one that says what you mean.

examples.en: I think the task will be manageable.
I am going to cancel an unnecessary trip.
We are joining a worthwhile activity tomorrow.
I think Tom will show up on time.
We are heading out at eight tomorrow.

drill.why: There is an agreement and a time: am / is / are + -ing.

fixes.wrong: I think the humidity will to rise.
fixes.right: I think the humidity will rise.

fixes.wrong: I think the humidity will rises.
fixes.right: I think the humidity will rise.

fixes.wrong: I think the beach will overcrowded.
fixes.right: I think the beach will be overcrowded.

fixes.wrong: Shall I to cool down the soup?
fixes.right: Shall I cool down the soup?

blocks.text: After will, I'll and Shall I always comes the action as in the dictionary: no to, no -s, no -ing. If a describing word follows, put be first.
You think it will happen — I think … will. You decide now or promise — I'll. You offer help — I'll or Shall I…? You decided earlier — going to; agreed a time — -ing.

examples.en: I think the holiday will be memorable.
I'll wipe down the table.
Shall I go over the list with you?
examples.translation: an offer to check it together
